svg.title: Cell biology overview
svg.desc: Cell structure: Animal cells: nucleus → DNA; cytoplasm → reactions; membrane → controls entry and exit. Mitochondria → aerobic respiration; ribosomes → protein synthesis. Plant cells: cellulose wall → strength; permanent vacuole → cell sap; photosynthetic cells have chloroplasts → photosynthesis. Bacteria: smaller, prokaryotic; no nucleus. Main DNA loop; some have plasmids. Membrane, cytoplasm and wall. Specialised cells: Structure → effect → function. Apply this link to unfamiliar cells too. Sperm: tail → swimming; mitochondria → energy; acrosome enzymes → penetrate egg's outer layers. Nerve: long fibre and branches → carry impulses and connect cells. Muscle: contractile proteins and mitochondria → contraction. Root hair: long extension → large absorption area; no chloroplasts normally. Xylem: hollow, lignified tubes → water transport and support. Phloem: sieve tubes and companion cells → sugar transport. Differentiation & stem cells: Differentiation: cells become specialised. Most animal cells do this early; many plant cells can throughout life. Adult division mainly repairs and replaces cells. Stem cells: undifferentiated; divide and can differentiate. Embryonic → most human cell types; bone marrow → limited range, including blood cells; meristems → any plant cell type. Potential treatments: diabetes and paralysis. Therapeutic cloning → patient's genes → matched tissue avoids rejection. Weigh benefits against viral infection and ethical or religious objections. Plant clones → conserve rare species and grow useful crops. Microscopy: Magnification = image enlargement. Resolution = distinguish nearby points as separate. Electron microscopes have more of both → finer detail. Magnification = image size ÷ actual size. Use the same units; rearrange for image or actual size. 1 cm = 10 mm; 1 mm = 1,000 µm; 1 µm = 1,000 nm. Use standard form; a tenfold size difference is one order of magnitude. Practical: thin sample, stain, coverslip angled; low power first, then fine focus. Observe, draw and label plant and animal cells; include a magnification scale or scale bar. Culturing microorganisms: Binary fission: bacteria double with nutrients and suitable temperature. Grow in nutrient broth or as colonies on agar. Aseptic technique: sterilise medium, dishes and loop; cool loop. Tape lid at edges; invert plate; incubate at maximum 25°C in school. Practical: compare antibiotic or antiseptic discs; solvent control; keep conditions equal; repeat. Larger zone of inhibition → greater inhibition under these conditions. Zone area = πr²; radius = diameter ÷ 2. Use squared units. Population = starting number × 2ⁿ; n = time ÷ division time. Use standard form when appropriate. Chromosomes & mitosis: Chromosomes are DNA, carry many genes and normally occur in pairs in body cells. 1. Grow and copy: more sub-cellular structures; DNA replicates into two joined identical copies of each chromosome. 2. Mitosis: copies separate; one complete set moves to each end; nucleus divides. 3. Divide: cytoplasm and membrane divide → two genetically identical daughter cells, with the same chromosome number as the parent. For growth, development, repair and replacement. DNA copying happens before mitosis. Diffusion & exchange: Diffusion: net movement of gas or dissolved particles from high to low concentration. No energy from respiration. Examples: oxygen, carbon dioxide and urea. Faster with a steeper gradient, higher temperature and larger membrane area. Large organisms have lower surface area to volume ratio → need exchange surfaces and transport systems. Cube: SA = 6a²; volume = a³. Large area; thin barrier; good blood supply; ventilation → efficient exchange in animals. Alveoli, villi and gills have large areas. Root hairs increase absorption area; thin leaves and air spaces shorten gas diffusion paths. Osmosis & active transport: Osmosis: net water movement from dilute to concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane; no respiration energy needed. Water gain → plant cell turgid; water loss → flaccid. Animal cells can swell or shrink. Practical: equal-size plant samples in salt/sugar solutions; initial and final masses; blot, control conditions and repeat. % change = (final − initial) ÷ initial × 100. Rate = mass change ÷ time; graph's 0% crossing → no net water movement. Active transport: low → high concentration, against gradient; energy from respiration. Root mineral uptake and sugar absorption from gut into blood.

g.text: Dashed line = membrane; arrows show net movement
